title: Classically Realizable Incompatibility
authors: Songyi Liu, Yongjun Wang, Baoshan Wang, Yunyi Jia, Chang He
abstract: Incompatibility constitutes a fundamental aspect of quantum mechanics. However, not every quantum observable non-classical property arises from incompatibility, nor can all quantum scenarios be fully captured by incompatibility alone. Within the framework of partial Boolean algebra (pBA), we research the structural properties of incompatibility scenarios. We introduce a unified method to realize any incompatibility scenario via a classical game, and the construction is extendable to any scenario embeddable into a Boolean algebra. The exclusivity graph offers a precise characterization of incompatibility scenarios. We prove that every exclusivity graph is the atom graph of an exclusive pBA, which is embedded into a Boolean algebra. These results provide a necessary condition for exclusivity graphs and a sufficient condition for atom graphs.
summary: This paper analyzes incompatibility in quantum mechanics using partial Boolean algebras (pBAs) and introduces the 'exclusivity graph' as a structural tool. The main finding is that many incompatible scenarios can be mathematically shown to be equivalent to structures embeddable into classical Boolean algebras, suggesting that mere incompatibility alone does not guarantee non-classicality.
main_problem: The research investigates the structural properties of incompatibility scenarios in quantum mechanics and determines if these scenarios are fundamentally non-classical or can be realized classically.
main_result: Every exclusivity graph is proven to be the atom graph of an exclusive partial Boolean algebra (pBA), which can be embedded into a standard Boolean algebra, suggesting that many incompatible scenarios are classically realizable.
method: The authors use the mathematical framework of partial Boolean algebras (pBAs) and introduce the 'exclusivity graph' to precisely characterize incompatibility structures. They develop a unified method to map these abstract structures onto classical games.
model_or_system: The model is based on quantum observables whose incompatibilities are studied using pBAs, which capture the logical structure of measurement outcomes. The analysis compares this framework against standard Boolean algebras and known contextuality examples like the Peres-Mermin square.
key_observables: Incompatibility itself, exclusivity graphs, partial Boolean algebras (pBA), and atom graphs.
important_parameters: The specific case $(1, 2, 2)$ for two incompatible dichotomic observables is used as a primary example.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes that the logical structure of incompatibility can be captured by pBAs, and it notes limitations regarding the full characterization (necessary/sufficient conditions) for exclusivity graphs.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the partial Boolean algebra $A(1,2,2)$ for two observables, the associated exclusivity graph, and examples like the Peres-Mermin square demonstrating compatibility structures.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by establishing the pBA framework to study incompatibility. It introduces the exclusivity graph as a characterization tool, proves that these graphs correspond to specific types of pBAs (epBA), and concludes by showing how these structures can be mapped onto classical games.
why_interesting: This work provides deep structural insights into the mathematical foundations of quantum contextuality, which is crucial for understanding measurement limitations in any quantum system, including those studied in AMO physics or quantum information theory.
